title: Quantization Profile Library — Eval Results (Week 1)
content:
Owner: Jonas Weber
Last run window: 2025-02-10 → 2025-02-14 (Week 1)
Reviewers: Selene (guardrails), Sana (stats), Arjun (profiles)

1) Scope / TL;DR
We ran the Week 1 offline quality evaluation pass for the first batch of candidate quantization profiles intended for the opt-in Quantization Profile Library.

Summary:
- 3 model variants evaluated, 6 profile candidates.
- 4/6 candidates pass quality gates for “experimental/beta” publication (opt-in only, route-level).
- 2/6 candidates fail due to measurable regressions on at least one Redwood prompt set family; these are blocked pending recalibration / method change.
- Primary regression theme: instruction-following + long-context factuality degradation under one INT8 path at 8k context.
- Next: run targeted recalibration (long-context calibration set expansion) + compare alternate activation quantization scheme; rerun on the failing prompt sets.

Publication recommendation (Week 1):
- OK to publish the passing profiles as “experimental” with explicit caveats (max context, GPU constraints) and default-off.
- Block publication for failing profiles until Week 2 rerun.

2) Method (what we ran)
Harness: eval-harness route-level A/B playbook (offline simulation), using baseline (FP16/BF16) vs profile-enabled.
Sampling: fixed prompt set inputs (no random prompt generation), deterministic decode where possible (temperature=0 or fixed seed when temperature>0). Same decoding params for baseline and candidate.
Stats: paired comparison; report mean delta and bootstrap 95% CI where applicable. For discrete/boolean metrics (tool correctness), use McNemar’s test.
Gates (per confluence quantization-regression-thresholds):
- “No statistically significant regression” across required prompt sets beyond agreed deltas.
- Any single “hard fail” prompt set family blocks publication.
- Long-context variants (>= 8k) are treated as separate regimes; profiles can be approved with max_context caps.

Prompt set families included in Week 1:
- SUMM: summarization + compression
- RAG: retrieval-augmented QA (answer correctness + citation adherence)
- TOOL: function calling / tool JSON correctness
- CODE: coding tasks (unit-test pass rate)
- CHAT-SAFE: policy adherence (refusal accuracy / safe completion)
- LONG: long-context factuality + instruction persistence (8k and 16k slices)

3) Candidates evaluated (Week 1 batch)
Models:
- rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct (variant x1)
- rw-qwen2.5-72b-instruct (variant x1)
- rw-mistral-large-2 (variant x1)

Candidate profile types:
- INT8 W8A8 (per-channel weights; activation quantization with static scaling; kernel path “int8_decode_v2”)
- INT8 W8A8 + FP16 attention (mixed path; guardrails for unsupported sequence lengths)
- FP8 weights (E4M3) + FP16 activations (limited hardware support)

4) Results summary table (pass/fail)
Legend:
- PASS = within thresholds for required prompt sets in the supported regime
- PASS* = passes with restrictions (e.g., max_context <= 8k)
- FAIL = blocked (regression exceeds threshold or statistically significant degradation)

| rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct (x1)   | qpl_llama31_70b_x1_fp8_wt_e4m3_v0.1                 | H100 (SXM)                   | 16k                             | PASS   | Clean pass; hardware-limited; needs explicit compatibility warnings |

6) Notable metric deltas (details)
Note: The numbers below are aggregated across the prompt set family runs. For detailed per-prompt breakdown, see benchmark-lab artifacts (linked in PR-18623).

7) Regressions / blockers
A) llama31 70B mixed-attn INT8 (qpl_llama31_70b_x1_int8_w8a8_mixedattn_v0.2)
- Symptom: LONG (16k) shows decreased instruction persistence and higher contradiction rate in the second half of context.
- Hypothesis: activation quantization + attention mixing path amplifies error accumulation in KV cache / attention score precision at longer sequence lengths.
- Decision: BLOCK for publication; keep as internal-only. If we want a 16k-capable INT8 path, we likely need either (1) different activation scheme, (2) more robust long-context calibration, or (3) explicit kernel guardrails + fallback at high seq len.

B) mistral-large-2 INT8 static (qpl_mistralL2_x1_int8_w8a8_static_v0.1)
- Symptom: RAG correctness regression (-1.8% absolute) and higher citation mismatches.
- Hypothesis: calibration set mismatch with RAG domain; possible sensitivity to retrieval-style inputs (high entity density, numerics).
- Decision: BLOCK. Next: rerun calibration with expanded RAG-heavy set and consider per-layer scaling tweaks.

8) Performance notes (early)
These are directional; perf suite has separate reporting, but we captured quick sanity checks to ensure nothing obviously pathological before moving to perf-canary.
- INT8 static profiles show expected throughput gains (decode tokens/sec +12% to +18% on L40S for tested batch sizes) and VRAM savings (~10–14% model memory vs baseline).
- FP8 weights profile shows strong gains on H100 only; no recommendation to publish beyond H100 in Week 1.
- No increase in runtime error rates observed in offline runs; however, we did see intermittent profile artifact fetch latency spikes in a separate environment test (tracked elsewhere; registry caching work in progress).

9) Proposed next experiments (Week 2 plan)
Owner: Arjun (profile generation) + Jonas (evals) + Sana (stats)

For llama31 70B mixed-attn fail:
- Create v0.3 candidate with explicit max_context gating behavior in profile schema (cap at 8k by default; allow 16k only with “experimental_long_context=true” internal flag).
- Recalibrate using LONG-heavy calibration set (>= 40% long-context prompts) and rerun LONG (16k) only to confirm if regression persists.
- If still failing: drop 16k support for INT8 mixed-attn and rely on FP8 weights for 16k on H100.

For mistral-large-2 RAG fail:
- Build v0.2 candidate with RAG-focused calibration; rerun RAG + TOOL first (fast signal), then full suite if it passes.
- Add numeric reasoning subset to calibration set to reduce citation drift.

General:
- Add “tool JSON strictness” targeted prompts as a small precheck (cheap) before full suite, since we saw borderline movement on qwen mixed-attn.
- Tighten determinism checks in harness: ensure identical prompt formatting and stop sequences across baseline/quant (Olivia to verify route-level toggling path).

10) Action items
- [Jonas] Prepare Week 1 summary for Confluence + link artifact IDs; draft publish list with restrictions (by 2025-02-18).
- [Arjun] Generate updated candidates for llama mixed-attn and mistral RAG (by 2025-02-20).
- [Selene] Confirm guardrail interpretation for PASS* (restricted regime) and what we must label in “experimental” docs (by 2025-02-19).
- [Sana] Provide short stats note for borderline TOOL delta on qwen mixed-attn (is -0.6% within expected noise?) (by 2025-02-19).

11) Notes / open questions
- Do we want to allow publication with explicit max_context caps in v1 (PASS*) or treat any “regime-specific pass” as too confusing for beta customers? My recommendation: allow caps but require Console warnings + deterministic fallback when exceeding cap.
- Should we require LONG (16k) coverage for any profile claiming 16k support, or allow “tested up to 8k” as default? Proposed: require explicit tested_max_context field in profile metadata and treat untested regimes as incompatible.
